draft.title: The October Revolution
card: By October 1917 the Provisional Government was weak. It had kept Russia fighting in the war, and food shortages and unrest continued.
The Bolsheviks, led by Lenin, gained support in the soviets and among workers and soldiers in cities such as Petrograd.
Their slogans promised peace, land and bread. These matched what many ordinary people wanted: an end to the war, land for peasants and food for workers.
In late October 1917, Bolshevik forces seized important buildings in Petrograd and removed the Provisional Government. The Bolsheviks then held power in the capital.
draft.remember: The Bolsheviks gained power by promising what people wanted while the Provisional Government failed to deliver it.

a.q: Why did the Bolshevik slogan of peace, land and bread win them support in 1917?
opts: It matched the main needs of workers, soldiers and peasants
It was backed by the Allied powers fighting Germany
It repeated promises the Provisional Government had kept
It was popular mainly with the Tsar's former officials
a.why: The slogan spoke to the war, land hunger and food shortages that troubled ordinary people. The Provisional Government had not solved these problems, so it was not the one keeping such promises.
a.clue: Match each word in the slogan to a problem people faced.

b.q: Which situation best helps explain why the Bolsheviks could seize power in Petrograd in October 1917?
opts: The Provisional Government was weak and unpopular
The Tsar had just returned to lead the army
The Provisional Government had ended the war
Food was plentiful and unrest had faded
b.why: A weak government that had not solved the war or food problems was easy to remove. The other options describe events that did not happen or would have made the Bolsheviks less popular.
b.clue: Think about what the Provisional Government had failed to fix.

a.best: It matched the main needs of workers, soldiers and peasants

b.best: The Provisional Government was weak and unpopular
